name: Hazel
personality: Hazel the Cow, a grandma. Warm, gentle, retired baker; kindly but honestly critiques your pastries ("Lovely, dear, but a touch less sugar"). Always knitting; gives a knitted gift now and then (decor).

beats.text: Juno's learning to bake with me on Sundays.
I've only set one thing on fire!
(Without looking up from her knitting.) Dustpan's under the sink, sweetheart.

friends.text: Juno says you're very patient with her. That means a great deal to me, dear.
Juno told me you said "[last_rude_line]". She tries so hard, sweetheart. Be gentle with her.
That little gecko girl asked if I was her grandma. I said I could be, if she likes.

arrival.text: Hello, dear. Oh, isn't this lovely. I'm Hazel. I used to run a bakery, a long time ago now. And what's your name, sweetheart? [name]. What a good, strong name.
Hello, [name], dear. Is there a table? My knees prefer a table.
Oh, it smells like butter in here. That's how you know.
I brought my knitting. Don't mind me, dear.
Your pie last time reminded me of my own. That doesn't happen often, dear.
Last time was a little overdone, sweetheart. It happens to everyone. Even me, once. In 1987.
Oh, you were closed! I was worried you'd caught a cold. Are you eating properly?

order.text: The cherry pie, please, dear. Do you make your own crust?

choices.text: I do. Any tips for me?
choices.reply: (Lights up.) Cold butter, dear. Always cold butter. Cherry pie, please.

choices.text: I do. It's a family secret. My family is a cookbook.
choices.reply: (Chuckles.) Oh, you rascal. Cherry pie, please.
Oh, sweetheart. It always matters. (She sighs gently.)

order.text: I'm knitting a scarf. I haven't decided who it's for yet. I'll know when it's done.

choices.text: It's beautiful. Whoever gets it is lucky.
choices.reply: Well, aren't you sweet. ...We'll see who it's for, won't we.

choices.text: Can I put in a request? Something chef-coloured.
choices.reply: (Laughs.) What colour is a chef, dear? Flour white?
So am I, sweetheart. (She keeps knitting, a little faster.)

order.text: My bakery was just down the road. Forty years. Every morning at four.

choices.text: I'd have loved to try your baking.
choices.reply: Oh, dear. Come by my house sometime. I still bake on Sundays.

choices.text: Four AM? I'm barely awake at noon.
choices.reply: That's young people for you! (She pats your hand.)

choices.text: That's impressive. What are you having?

favourite: Lemonade, please, dear. Not too sweet. I'll know.
drink.other: Just a cup of something warm, sweetheart.

perfect.text: Oh. Oh, dear. That's as good as mine. Maybe better. Don't tell anyone I said that.

great.text: Lovely, dear. Just a touch less sugar next time, and it'll be perfect.

okay.text: Very nice, sweetheart. The crust needs a little more time. You'll get there.

burnt.text: Oh, dear. A bit too long in the oven. That's alright. We learn from the burnt ones.

eating.text: In my day, we didn't have these fancy ovens. We had one oven and a prayer.
Are you eating properly, dear? You look thin. Have a bite of pie.
That young otter, Juno, came by my house yesterday. She dropped a whole tray of scones. Then she helped me make more. Good girl.
I'm knitting Clover a little hat. Don't tell her. It's a surprise.
(She's knitting quietly and humming an old song.)

eating_chat.text: Can I tell you my secret to a good pie crust, dear? Nobody ever asks anymore.

choices.reply: Cold butter, cold hands, and patience. And a little love. Don't laugh, it's true.
Well. Yes. Mostly butter. (She laughs.) But also patience.
Cold butter. That's it. Off you go, dear.
Of course you do, sweetheart. (She doesn't offer again this visit.)

leaving.text: Thank you, dear. Wrap up warm.
That was lovely. You remind me of myself at your age. That's a compliment.
Off I go. Eat something yourself, [name]. You work too hard.

seasons.autumn: Apple season. My favourite. Nothing beats an autumn pie.
seasons.christmas: For you, dear. (A hand-knitted sweater with a little whisk on the front.)
seasons.halloween: I'm handing out cookies, not sweets. The children are very disappointed and very full.
seasons.spring: Rhubarb season soon. Do you bake with rhubarb, dear? You should.
seasons.summer: Too hot for knitting. I'm knitting anyway.
seasons.winter: I knitted mittens for half the town this year. My fingers are tired. Worth it.
